overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a mild late-June day with the temperature sitting at 66.2°F as of 10:50 ET under partly sunny skies with a light south wind. The running max was recorded as early as 09:10 ET, though intraday dynamics still show a slight positive 2-hour velocity (+0.9°F/hr) suggesting some afternoon warming potential remains. The negative acceleration (-0.9°F/hr²) and flattening recent trend indicate the pace of warming is slowing considerably.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable spread among models: ECMWF (71.2°F) and HRRR (71.6°F) cluster together about 2–4°F above the NWS text forecast of 69°F, while NBM (67.2°F) aligns closer to NWS. Current observations at 66.2°F are tracking slightly below even the most conservative model (NBM), though meaningful peak timing is still projected several hours out (model mean ~17.7h ET). The INTRADAY model shows an anomalous probability spike in the 84–95°F range that is clearly inconsistent with observations and should be discounted; the META model's concentration in 72–75°F appears more credible but may still be slightly warm given the early morning max and decelerating trend.
max_temp_prediction: Balancing the NWS forecast (69°F), NWP model consensus (ECMWF/HRRR ~71°F, NBM ~67°F), current running max of 66.2°F with roughly 4+ hours to go before typical peak, and the slowing warming rate, the most probable outcome is a daily high in the 69–72°F range. The META model's modal buckets of 72–73°F (36.9%) and 74–75°F (34.4%) may overstate the upside given observed deceleration. Confidence is moderate-low given model spread and an unusually early morning temperature peak; best single estimate is near 70.5°F with the bulk of risk skewed slightly to the downside relative to ECMWF/HRRR.
